===== grok --version =====
grok 1.0.77 (50ca579fa996)

===== grok --help =====
Grok Build TUI

Usage: grok [OPTIONS] [PROMPT] [COMMAND]

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]  Initial prompt for the interactive session

Options:
      --add-dir <DIR>
          Also work in this folder, beside the working directory (repeatable)
      --agent <NAME>
          Agent name or definition file path
      --agents <JSON>
          Inline subagent definitions as JSON
      --allow <RULE>
          Permission allow rule (compat aliases: --allowedTools, --allowed-tools)
      --always-approve
          Auto-approve all tool executions
  -c, --continue
          Continue the most recent session for the current working directory
      --cwd <CWD>
          Working directory
      --debug
          Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE
      --deny <RULE>
          Permission deny rule (compat alias: --disallowedTools)
      --disable-web-search
          Disable web search and web fetch tools
      --disallowed-tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to remove (comma-separated)
      --fork-session
          When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original
      --fullscreen
          Open in the standard fullscreen TUI for this session
  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with 'grok help')
      --include-partial-messages
          Emit incremental text and thinking deltas alongside whole messages
      --json-schema <SCHEMA>
          JSON Schema for structured output
      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`
  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model ID to use
      --max-turns <N>
          Maximum number of agent turns
      --minimal
          Experimental: scrollback-native rendering
      --no-alt-screen
          Run inline instead of using the terminal alternate screen
      --no-plan
          Disable plan mode
      --no-subagents
          Disable subagent spawning
      --oauth
          Force browser (loopback) login when the welcome screen authenticates
      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
          Output format for headless mode [default: plain] [possible values: plain, json, streaming-json, streaming-messages-json]
  -p, --single <PROMPT>
          Single-turn prompt. Prints the response to stdout and exits
      --permission-mode <MODE>
          Permission mode [possible values: default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan]
      --prompt-file <PATH>
          Single-turn prompt from a file
      --prompt-json <JSON>
          Single-turn prompt as JSON content blocks
  -r, --resume [<SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>]
          Resume a session by ID or title, or the most recent if omitted
      --reasoning-effort <EFFORT>
          Reasoning effort for reasoning models [aliases: --effort]
      --restore-code
          Restore the original session's repository snapshot when resuming
      --rules <RULES>
          Extra rules to append to the system prompt
  -s, --session-id <SESSION_ID>
          Use a specific session UUID for a new conversation
      --sandbox <PROFILE>
          Sandbox profile for filesystem and network access [env: GROK_SANDBOX=]
      --system-prompt-override <PROMPT>
          Override the agent's system prompt (compat alias: --system-prompt)
      --tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to allow (comma-separated)
  -v, --version
          Print version
      --verbatim
          Send the prompt exactly as given
  -w, --worktree [<WORKTREE>]
          Start the session in a new git worktree, optionally named
      --worktree-ref <WORKTREE_REF>
          Branch, tag, or commit to base the worktree on (with `--worktree`) [aliases: --ref]

Commands:
  agent        Run Grok without the interactive UI
  clone        Lazy-clone a git repository via grove (NFS on macOS, FUSE on Linux)
  completions  Generate shell completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, ...)
  dashboard    Open the Agent Dashboard view at startup
  doctor       Check terminal, clipboard, color, and input support without starting Grok
  du           Show what the grok home (~/.grok) uses on disk [aliases: disk-usage]
  export       Export a session transcript as Markdown
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
  inspect      Show the configuration Grok discovers for this directory
  leader       Manage running leader processes
  login        Sign in to Grok
  logout       Sign out and clear cached credentials
  mcp          Manage MCP server configurations
  memory       Manage cross-session memory
  models       List available models and exit
  plugin       Manage plugins and marketplace sources
  sessions     List, search, or restore sessions
  setup        Fetch and install managed configuration
  trace        Export or upload session trace data
  update       Check for updates or install a specific version
  usage        Print your plan's usage limit, or a session's persisted token and cost usage
  version      Print version information [aliases: v]
  worker       Run this machine as a Cursor private worker
  worktree     Manage git worktrees
  wrap         Run any command with local clipboard support

===== grok login --help =====
Sign in to Grok

Usage: grok login [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --oauth
          Force browser (loopback) login instead of device-code authentication

      --device-auth
          Use device-code authentication for headless/remote environments
          
          [aliases: --device-code]

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. When the leader runs a shared daemon, the daemon listens beside PATH at `PATH.daemon`

===== grok usage --help =====
Print your plan's usage limit, or a session's persisted token and cost usage

Usage: grok usage [OPTIONS] [SESSION_ID] [TURN]

Arguments:
  [SESSION_ID]
          Session ID. Omit for your plan's usage limit (needs Grok's background service)

  [TURN]
          Turn number. Omit for session totals and every recorded turn

Options:
      --json
          Print the plan's usage limit as JSON

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. When the leader runs a shared daemon, the daemon listens beside PATH at `PATH.daemon`

===== grok worker --help =====
Run this machine as a Cursor private worker

Usage: grok worker [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start       Run a leader in this terminal until Ctrl+C
  stop        Unregister from Cursor and release the claims (the leader keeps running)
  status      Show the current worker status and its Cloud Agent claims [aliases: list]
  controller  Claim pending Cloud Agent requests for team pools and run a spawn hook for each
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Worker display name shown in Cursor [env: CURSOR_WORKER_NAME=]
      --worker-dir <DIR>
          Repository directory offered to Cursor Cloud Agents
      --max-agents <N>
          Maximum concurrent Cloud Agent claims
      --pool [<NAME>]
          Join a team Self-Hosted Pool
      --single-use
          Same as `--pool` (legacy alias)
      --pool-name <NAME>
          Deprecated alias for `--pool <NAME>`. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`
      --mint-github-token
          Let Cursor send the pool worker short-lived GitHub tokens during a claimed run
      --sync-dashboard-secrets
          Let Cursor send the pool worker the team's dashboard secrets as env variables
      --clone-git-repos
          Clone the claimed run's repository with the minted token
      --label <KEY=VALUE>
          Routing label for the worker, as `key=value`. Repeatable
      --labels-file <PATH>
          JSON or TOML file of worker labels. Cannot be combined with `--label` [env: CURSOR_WORKER_LABELS_FILE=]
      --api-key <KEY>
          Cursor API key the worker registers with, in place of your linked Cursor account [env: CURSOR_API_KEY]
      --auth-token-file <PATH>
          File holding the worker's Cursor auth token, re-read before every reconnect
      --on-session-start <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim lands. Needs `--pool`
      --on-session-end <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim is released. Needs `--pool`
      --identity-socket
          Give each Cloud Agent its own OIDC identity socket
      --management-addr <ADDRESS>
          Serve worker health over HTTP for Kubernetes probes
      --run-mcp-servers
          Run each Cloud Agent's stdio MCP servers on this pool worker
      --mcp-tool-timeout <SERVER[/TOOL]=SECONDS>
          How long a tool call to a stdio MCP server this worker runs may take. Repeatable
      --idle-release-timeout <SECONDS>
          Seconds a claim may sit idle before Cursor releases it. 0 turns this off [env: CURSOR_WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=]
      --data-dir <DIR>
          Directory for this worker's state, served by its own leader
      --wait [<SECONDS>]
          Wait for the leader already running on the worker's socket to stop, then start
      --debug
          Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with 'grok help worker')
      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

===== grok worker controller --help =====
Claim pending Cloud Agent requests for team pools and run a spawn hook for each.

Watches the pending-request stream of each `--pool` (or the whole team with `--all-pools`), claims each new request for a fresh worker id, and runs `--spawn` once per claim. The hook gets `CURSOR_AGENT_WORKER_ID`, `CURSOR_POOL`, `CURSOR_API_KEY` (or `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN` with `--session-token`) and the request's fields, and should start `grok worker --pool "$CURSOR_POOL" start` somewhere. That worker needs Grok Build unified: start it with `GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1` unless the build embeds the agent-host daemon. A sleeping machine in a pool with a wake window runs the hook again with `CURSOR_WAKE=1`, `CURSOR_WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` and its own worker id, without a claim. With `--warm-idle` the controller never claims: it keeps idle workers connected in each `--pool`, and the server assigns queued requests to them. Logs go to stderr at info level; `RUST_LOG` overrides that. Authenticates with a team service account key (`--api-key` or `CURSOR_API_KEY`).

Usage: grok worker controller [OPTIONS] --spawn <PATH>

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Worker display name shown in Cursor.
          
          Default: `[cursor_worker].name`, then the hostname.
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_NAME=]

      --spawn <PATH>
          Hook to run once per claimed request or missing warm worker.
          
          A claim's hook gets the request in its environment; a warm worker's hook gets none. The hook must exit 0 within 60 seconds, so it should start the worker in the background. A hook that fails or runs longer is killed with everything it started, and the claim is released back to the queue.

      --pool <NAME>
          Pool to watch, or to keep warm with `--warm-idle`. Repeatable.
          
          Without `--warm-idle`, pools other than `default` are registered at startup. Cannot be combined with `--all-pools`.

      --worker-dir <DIR>
          Repository directory offered to Cursor Cloud Agents.
          
          Repeatable (default: `[cursor_worker].worker_dirs`, then the current directory unless `[cursor_worker] any_repo = true`). The first one is the registered working directory.

      --all-pools
          Watch every pool of the team, without registering any

      --max-agents <N>
          Maximum concurrent Cloud Agent claims.
          
          Default: `[cursor_worker].max_agents`; unset means no cap.

      --repository <URL>
          Only take requests for this repository URL. Required for repository-scoped keys.
          
          Also pins the pools registered at startup to the repository, and warm mode's idle count to the workers serving it.

      --session-token
          Give the hook a token that serves only its claim, in place of the API key.
          
          The hook gets `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN` and `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_AT`; write the token to a file and start the worker with `--auth-token-file`. Needs private-worker session tokens enabled for the team.

      --single-use
          Same as `--pool` (legacy alias)

      --identity-audience <AUD>
          Ask each claim for a signed identity token bound to this audience.
          
          The hook gets `CURSOR_IDENTITY_TOKEN`, `CURSOR_IDENTITY_TOKEN_EXPIRES_AT` and `CURSOR_IDENTITY_NONCE` to check the user before it starts a worker. A wake makes no claim, so its hook gets no identity token.

      --pool-name <NAME>
          Deprecated alias for `--pool <NAME>`. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`.
          
          `CURSOR_WORKER_POOL_NAME` names the pool of a bare `--pool` or `--single-use` and is ignored otherwise.

      --mint-github-token
          Let Cursor send the pool worker short-lived GitHub tokens during a claimed run.
          
          Needs `--pool`. A team admin must turn on GitHub token minting for pool workers. Without this flag, the worker refuses the tokens. The worker redacts the token from what the agent sees, best effort.

      --warm-idle <COUNT>
          Keep this many idle workers connected in each `--pool`, without claiming.
          
          Runs `--spawn` once per missing worker, with a fresh `CURSOR_AGENT_WORKER_ID`, the pool, the API key and the `--repository` if one is given, and no request; the server assigns queued requests to the idle workers. Idle counts come from the team's pool stats, read every minute and after stream events. At most 100. Needs `--pool`; cannot be combined with `--all-pools`, `--session-token` or `--identity-audience`. Run one warm controller per pool: without claims, two can spawn more workers than needed.

      --endpoint <URL>
          Cursor public API base for the claim calls and the hook's `CURSOR_API_URL`.
          
          Not read from `CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT`, which Grok Build uses for the agent host's backend.
          
          [default: https://api.cursor.com]

      --sync-dashboard-secrets
          Let Cursor send the pool worker the team's dashboard secrets as env variables.
          
          They arrive during a claimed run. Needs `--pool`. A team admin must turn on dashboard secret sync for pool workers. The worker redacts them from what the agent sees, best effort.

      --clone-git-repos
          Clone the claimed run's repository with the minted token.
          
          For an any-repo pool worker: a named `--pool` other than `default`, a `--worker-dir` that is not a git checkout with an origin, and no `repo=` or `name=` label. Clones go under the worker's own directory in the Grok home, never into the worker dir; a clone of the same repository there is reused and fetched. Implies `--mint-github-token`.

      --label <KEY=VALUE>
          Routing label for the worker, as `key=value`. Repeatable

      --labels-file <PATH>
          JSON or TOML file of worker labels. Cannot be combined with `--label`
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_LABELS_FILE=]

      --api-key <KEY>
          Cursor API key the worker registers with, in place of your linked Cursor account.
          
          Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`), as does `--auth-token-file`. Prefer `CURSOR_API_KEY`: other local users can read a key passed here in the process list.
          
          [env: CURSOR_API_KEY]

      --auth-token-file <PATH>
          File holding the worker's Cursor auth token, re-read before every reconnect.
          
          The file holds only the token; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Takes precedence over `--api-key`.

      --on-session-start <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim lands. Needs `--pool`.
          
          Runs with `sh -c` in your home directory and gets the session as JSON on stdin. `CURSOR_WORKER_BC_ID` names the agent run. A JSON reply with an `env` object sets variables for the `--on-session-end` command. Stopped after 60 seconds; a failure is logged and never holds up the claim.

      --on-session-end <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim is released. Needs `--pool`.
          
          Runs with `sh -c` in your home directory, after `--on-session-start` finishes, and gets the session and its end `reason` as JSON on stdin. The worker recycles after it finishes, or after 60 seconds; stopping the worker gives it only 5 seconds. A failure is logged and never holds up the teardown.

      --identity-socket
          Give each Cloud Agent its own OIDC identity socket.
          
          Its shells get the path as `CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET`. An agent POSTs to `/v1/tokens/oidc` on it to mint a short-lived Cursor cloud-agent identity token for an audience it names. Off by default; no socket exists without it. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).

      --management-addr <ADDRESS>
          Serve worker health over HTTP for Kubernetes probes.
          
          ADDRESS is `:8080` (every IPv4 address) or `host:8080`. `GET /healthz` answers 200 while the worker runs, and 503 once it has stopped for good (a rejected credential). `GET /readyz` answers 200 when the worker is connected to Cursor, holds no claim and is not shutting down, and 503 otherwise; its JSON body reports each of those. The worker fails to start when it cannot bind ADDRESS. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).

      --run-mcp-servers
          Run each Cloud Agent's stdio MCP servers on this pool worker.
          
          A personal worker always runs them, as the Cursor CLI's does. A pool worker runs them only with this flag, because they are commands from any member of the team. They start in the claim's worktree with its environment, without the worker's Cursor credentials. A worker that runs them also offers every claim the stdio servers in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, as the Cursor CLI's does. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`.

      --mcp-tool-timeout <SERVER[/TOOL]=SECONDS>
          How long a tool call to a stdio MCP server this worker runs may take. Repeatable.
          
          `SERVER=SECONDS` covers every tool of that server; `SERVER/TOOL=SECONDS` covers one tool and wins over the server's value. A later value for the same server or tool replaces an earlier one, and `0` fails each call without waiting. SERVER is the name in the claim's MCP config, which the worker logs when it starts the server. Without it a call fails after the MCP SDK's 60 seconds; Cursor itself stops waiting after about 14 minutes. A `--pool` worker also needs `--run-mcp-servers`. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).

      --idle-release-timeout <SECONDS>
          Seconds a claim may sit idle before Cursor releases it. 0 turns this off.
          
          Defaults to 3600 for a `--pool` worker, which stops once released, and to 0 otherwise. Cursor still releases claims for its other reasons. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=]

      --data-dir <DIR>
          Directory for this worker's state, served by its own leader.
          
          Holds the worker ids, Cursor session, claim worktrees and clones that otherwise live in the Grok home, so it must be another directory. The leader listens at `DIR/leader.sock`, so each data directory runs one worker, as in the Cursor CLI; `--leader-socket` cannot name another socket. `grok worker status` and `stop` with the same directory reach that leader. Unlike the Cursor CLI, `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` is not read. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`), as does `--wait`.

      --wait [<SECONDS>]
          Wait for the leader already running on the worker's socket to stop, then start.
          
          The socket is `--data-dir`'s, else `--leader-socket`, else the default one that every `grok --leader` shares, whose leader stays up while any of them is connected. Without SECONDS, waits as long as it takes; with SECONDS, fails once they pass. Without `--wait`, `start` leaves a running leader alone.

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. When the leader runs a shared daemon, the daemon listens beside PATH at `PATH.daemon`
